label: PF Backlog 603
title: EDP-22: Benchmarks/SLOs + EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) tuning + observability + quotas + graceful degradation (DB/object/cache/queue)

brief.problem: No repeatable performance baselines, SLOs, or degradation strategy exist across DB/object/cache/queue.
brief.what_adds: Benchmark harness, EXPLAIN-based tuning, observability, quotas, and graceful degradation switches.
brief.why: Enterprise scale claims need evidence and operational guardrails.
brief.who_feels: Operators, SREs, and customers hitting slow paths.

objective: Establish performance benchmarks/SLOs, EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS)-based tuning, observability, quotas, and graceful degradation for DB, object store, cache, and queue.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark suite produces repeatable results for each store with recorded baselines
EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture tooling available and sampling-only in prod
Quota enforcement and degradation switches demonstrated per store
out_of_scope: Data-model changes of the stores themselves
approach: Define workload scenarios, capture EXPLAIN baselines, wire metrics, add quota checks and store-specific degradation switches.

prior_decisions: EDP-06 baseline harness landed with a Sink seam reserved for EDP-22.
EDP-19/20/21 stores and EDP-18 migration framework are complete.
assumptions: SLO numbers are set from measured local baselines first.
divergences: EDP-22 does not add replicas or partitioning; it produces the evidence those decisions require.
open_questions: Which deployment-specific SLO targets should override conservative defaults?

impact_review.claim: API CHECK: no new public API; benchmark CLI and ops tooling only.
AC CHECK: four acceptance criteria mapped to four slices.
LANGUAGE CHECK: shipped performance tooling in Go; EXPLAIN helper in Python tooling.
SLO CHECK: bounded metric labels per store/scenario; no tenant labels.
DEGRADATION CHECK: switches must fail closed and be observable.

verification: benchmark CLI produces baseline JSON and Prometheus text
risks: SLO thresholds can be aspirational without measured baselines.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE must be sampling-only in production.
Degradation switches can mask failures if not bounded and alerted.
Benchmark scenarios must remain deterministic and tenant-safe.
rollback: Benchmarks and metrics are additive; degradation switches default off and can be disabled per store.
evidence: Candidate analyzers show existing analysis patterns

analysis.implementation_strategy: Build a perf/observability capability: benchmark harness reusing core/code_analyzer.py and core/product_analyzer.py patterns, EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture tooling, metric emission on DB/object/cache/queue, quota enforcement hooks, and degradation switches on each store.
dependency_findings: BLOCKS nothing; later items benefit from SLOs
conflict_findings: Touches read/write paths of every store — sequence strictly after EDP-19..21 land
Concurrent edit risk with BI-PF-1315 reconciliation probes
duplication_findings: core/code_analyzer.py/product_analyzer.py are analyzers, not perf harnesses — only reuse metric/format patterns
BI-PF-1312 audit metrics may overlap — reuse rather than re-instrument
analysis.rationale: Cross-cutting performance capability that must follow all store work; classified as new capability since no existing benchmarking component fits.
assumptions: Stores expose queryable interfaces after EDP-19..21
Metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTel) exists or is in scope-lite
risks: No baseline metrics exist — SLO targets may be aspirational
EXPLAIN overhead must be sampling-only in prod
evidence: Candidate analyzers show existing analysis patterns
missing_info: Target SLO numbers and acceptable latency budgets
Existing metrics/observability stack to plug into

context_review.reason: Approach is clear but depends on upstream EDP-19..21 stores landing first.

api_impact.reason: Internal benchmark CLI, SLO rules, and ops tooling; no product API surface.

tier_reasons: cross-cutting DB/object/cache/queue performance, SLO, quota, and degradation surface
language_rule: Go for shipped benchmark/SLO code; Python only for repo ops tooling.

requirements: Benchmark suite produces repeatable results for each store with recorded baselines
EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) capture tooling available and sampling-only in prod
Quota enforcement and degradation switches demonstrated per store
scope: Slice 1: benchmark CLI, versioned baseline artifacts, Prometheus SLO sink, SLO config/rules/dashboard.
Slice 2: EXPLAIN(ANALYZE,BUFFERS) sampling capture with read-only role, allowlist, timeout, rollback, and redaction.
Slice 3: per-store metrics + quota/degradation policy with bounded expiry and alerts.
Slice 4: measured baselines and evidence for DB/object/cache/queue.
non_goals: No read replicas, partitioning, or region cells (EDP-24).
No production EXPLAIN sampling without an explicit switch.
invariants: Benchmarks are deterministic, versioned, and tenant-safe; labels never include tenant IDs.
Benchmarks use PF_BENCH_DSN with a NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS read-only role.
Missing DSN fails closed unless --allow-skip records per-store skipped evidence.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE is production-sampled at <=0.05, read-only, allowlisted, timed out, rolled back, and redacted.
Degradation is bounded by max_duration, auto-expires, emits alerts, and never returns a zeroed success.
SLO thresholds come from a measured baseline with explicit variance tolerance.
Config is single-source: config/edp-slo.json generates rules/dashboard; config/edp-degradation.json is schema-validated.
Benchmark runs set app.tenant_id to a synthetic t-bench tenant and assert non-empty RLS-scoped reads.

api: No new public API; internal benchmark CLI only.
db: Uses existing stores; EXPLAIN ANALYZE only on sampled queries.

security: Bench/EXPLAIN DSN must be a read-only role (pf_readonly) with no superuser/bypassrls.
Benchmark labels exclude tenant IDs, DSNs, and secrets.
EXPLAIN uses static allowlisted SQL with no bound tenant parameters; output is redacted and access-controlled.
Degradation/config changes are operator-only; no public API.
Explain runs are recorded in an audit log with actor, statement label, sample decision, and artifact path; artifacts are access-controlled and retained per config.
observability: Benchmark metrics: edp_bench_p50_ms, p95, p99, errors, run_timestamp, with bounded group/scenario labels.
SLO rules are generated from config/edp-slo.json by scripts/dev/gen_edp_slo.py; Grafana rules are generated from the same source.
SLO rules include for-duration, freshness, latency regression, error rate, and degradation expiry alerts.
performance: Benchmark ops and concurrency are explicit CLI flags.
EXPLAIN sampling is capped and statement_timeout bounded.
No unbounded scans; baselines capture ops, concurrency, dataset size, host class, and duration.
rollout: Benchmark scheduling and EXPLAIN sampling default off.
Enable per environment with operator-owned config and runbooks.
rollback: Disable sampling/scheduling and remove rules/dashboard; no schema change.
decisions: Use measured local baselines before tightening SLO thresholds.
guardrails: Instrument existing adapters; no new store.
learnings: EDP-06 deferred the Sink intentionally; EDP-22 supplies it.
open_questions: Deployment-specific SLO overrides are schema-validated and applied only after a measured baseline; no thresholds are invented before measurement.

coverage.adapter: bench CLI + versioned baseline artifact + SLO sink
coverage.contract: six store groups mapped to explicit store enum; versioned baseline artifacts include git sha, host, ops, concurrency, duration, seed, variance tolerance; --allow-skip records non-success skipped evidence and must be gated by test; labels bounded
failure_cases: missing DSN -> fail unless explicit skip

coverage.adapter: explain capture policy + psycopg read-only capture
coverage.contract: static allowlist, read-only transaction, statement_timeout, rollback, production sample <=0.05, persistent operator switch, audit log, redaction, retention and access control
call_sites: operator -> cmd/explain -> explain.Capture -> rollback transaction + audit sink

coverage.contract: SLO rules generated from config/edp-slo.json; alerts/dashboard cover DB/object/cache/queue with owner, for-duration, freshness, error/latency, degradation expiry; store metrics emission tested
call_sites: store adapters -> observe metrics -> Prometheus -> Grafana/alerts

coverage.contract: quota hook and per-store switch share bounded policy: query quota, max_duration<=15m, auto-expiry, allowed/denied metrics with bounded scope/store labels, fixed degraded error, alert routing
call_sites: store adapter -> limits.Quota + degrade.Policy -> bounded error + metrics

proof_plan.red_evidence: Baseline CLI/SLO sink absent; EXPLAIN guard absent; degradation policy absent.
proof_plan.green_evidence: Benchmark CLI/SLO, EXPLAIN guard, store metrics, and degradation tests pass with measured baselines.

runtime_contract.trigger: scheduled operator benchmark or sampled EXPLAIN request
runtime_contract.adapter: edpsvc bench + Prometheus/Grafana + psycopg EXPLAIN tool
runtime_contract.contract: bounded, versioned baselines and sampled plans; no tenant labels
runtime_contract.failure_behavior: fail closed on regression/unsampled prod; fixed degradation errors
runtime_contract.observable_result: operators see latency/error/freshness/degradation alerts per store

api_contract: See EDP-22 design: no new schema; bounded labels; sampling-only EXPLAIN; degradation fail-closed.
audit: Benchmark runs, sampling decisions, redaction, and degradation start/expiry are logged/auditable.
backup_restore: No data-model change; benchmark and EXPLAIN artifacts follow existing backup/retention.
compatibility: New internal CLI/config; no public API change.
concurrency_idempotency: Baseline compare is deterministic for a fixed seed; EXPLAIN is read-only.
data_model: No new database schema; benchmark artifacts are versioned files/objects; EXPLAIN captures are retained artifacts with access control.
deployment_rollout: Benchmark schedule and EXPLAIN sampling default off; operators enable with config and runbook.
Degradation requires owner, reason, max_duration<=15m, and auto-expiry; alert on start/expiry.
ownership: edpsvc owns bench/SLO/degrade; ops owns sample execution and dashboards.
performance_capacity: Measured baselines define thresholds; explicit ops/concurrency; bounded sampling.
prerequisites: EDP-06 Sink seam; EDP-19/20/21 stores; EDP-18 migration tooling.
quotas: Per-store quota denied/allowed counters; degradation is bounded and expires automatically.
rls_tenant: Bench/EXPLAIN DSNs use read-only non-bypass roles; no tenant parameters in EXPLAIN; labels contain no tenant IDs.
rollback_recovery: Disable benchmarks/sampling; remove rules/dashboard; degradation auto-expires.
security_model: Read-only least-privilege DB roles; redacted plans; operator-only controls.

BLOCKER: AC-3 is not designed: open question on whether object/cache/queue expose counters means per-store SLO dashboards/alerts cannot be shown to exist; no adapter instrumentation files are in scope.
AC-4 is not designed: quota enforcement and per-store degradation switches reference `go/edpsvc/internal/limits` but no affected file, config schema, or test defines quotas/switch behavior per store.
DB access for benchmark and EXPLAIN capture has no least-privilege/read-only role or RLS enforcement; “tenant-safe” invariant lacks a boundary control and risks admin/RLS-bypass DSNs.
MAJOR: AC-1 lacks baseline artifact definition: no storage location, versioning, environment fingerprint, variance tolerance, or retention for recorded baselines, so repeatability is not verifiable.
AC-1 failure case “missing DSN -> skipped scenarios” can produce a green run without per-store coverage; it should fail closed or record explicit skipped-store evidence.
AC-2 prod enforcement is underspecified: no environment detection and no hard production cap preventing `sample_rate=1.0`; sampling-only policy can be bypassed by config.
AC-2 `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes statements; no read-only transaction, statement allowlist, statement timeout, or rollback guard is defined.
AC-2 redaction of parameters/tenant data is declared but has no mechanism or test evidence; captured plans can leak literals/tenant data.
AC-3 validation is weak: Python config tests do not prove Prometheus rule semantics, alert lead time, or Grafana dashboard/schema validity; scrape/eval intervals remain open.
AC-4 “bounded” degradation is not quantified: no max duration, auto-expiry, quota-denied metric, or alert-routing handoff is defined.
SLO thresholds are not tied to measured baselines; open deployment overrides and aspirational values risk alert noise or missed regressions.
MINOR: Benchmark reconstruction metadata is incomplete: concurrency, dataset seed/size, host class, and run duration should be recorded with baselines.
Mixing SLO policy and runtime quota/degradation policy in `config/edp-slo.json` blurs ownership and rollback boundaries.
Captured EXPLAIN artifacts need explicit retention and access-control policy beyond “redacted”.
Quota enforcement observability lacks clear denied/allowed counters and bounded store labels.
NIT: `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py` is acceptable as tooling, but its prod guardrails should be documented alongside ops runbooks.
Single evidence doc `docs/EDP-22-BENCHMARKS-SLOS.md` should index baseline artifacts, rule files, dashboards, and per-store proof.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound on bounded labels, fail-closed regression, and default-off rollout, but AC-3 and AC-4 are not yet demonstrable.
Top risks: missing per-store SLO/counter coverage, undefined quota/degradation implementation evidence, and insufficient DB privilege/RLS and EXPLAIN redaction controls.
AC-1/AC-2 need stronger repeatability, environment, sampling, and read-only execution contracts before Gate 1.5.

BLOCKER: AC-4 quota enforcement is not designed: no quota hook in `affected_files`, `call_sites`, or test matrix; `limits/quota.go` is only cited as evidence and remains out of scope, so “quota enforcement … demonstrated per store” cannot pass.

AC-1 can pass without per-store baselines: `--allow-skip` records skipped evidence but no gate/test rejects it, and the test matrix is only `go test ./...` with no repeat-run/variance or baseline-artifact validation.
MAJOR: AC-3/AC-4 review scope omits `go/edpsvc/internal/observe/metrics.go` and `go/edpsvc/internal/degrade/policy.go`, the declared entrypoints for store metrics and degradation; the binding review cannot verify those ACs.
AC-3 test matrix covers only `test_edp_slo_config.py`; `metrics_test.go` exists but store metric emission from `observe/metrics.go` is not part of AC-3 evidence.

AC-2 production EXPLAIN sampling relies on operator-run `scripts/dev/db_explain_capture.py`; no deployment path, persistent sampling switch, audit sink, access-control enforcement, or retention control is designed beyond assertions.

Benchmark tenant safety is underspecified: no synthetic tenant/fixture or RLS session context is defined, so a NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS role with no tenant parameters may produce empty/error benchmarks or rely on unforced RLS.
SLO thresholds exist in both `config/edp-slo.json` and `ops/prometheus/edp-slo.rules.yml`; no single-source generation/contract is stated, so config/rule drift is likely.
MINOR: `edp_quota_denials_total{scope,store}` leaves `scope` undefined; if not allowlisted it is a high-cardinality label risk.
Failure matrix `BENCH_DSN_MISSING` wording/exit semantics are contradictory for `--allow-skip`; define whether skipped evidence is non-success.
Baseline and EXPLAIN artifact retention/access control are asserted but not specified in scoped files.
“Six store groups” vs DB/object/cache/queue mapping is unspecified; baseline artifact naming is not tied to a declared store enum.
No on-startup validation/compatibility check for `config/edp-slo.json` and `config/edp-degradation.json`; invalid config fails at runtime.
NIT: Metric naming mixes `edp_store_latency_ms_bucket` with `edp_bench_p95_ms`; ensure histogram/summary conventions are consistent.
`run_timestamp` in benchmark metrics may undermine baseline equality unless excluded from comparisons.
Docs are the only evidence for multiple ACs; add machine-checkable evidence references.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound: additive, read-only, bounded degradation, and no public API.
Gate-1 cannot approve AC-1/AC-4 as written; quota enforcement and repeatability/baseline evidence are materially missing.
Top risks: prod EXPLAIN sampling controls, metrics/degradation outside verifiable scope, and config/rule drift.
